title: Analytic Solutions To Fully Quantized Parametric Amplification
abstract: We derive analytic expressions for observable dynamics under the fully quantized trilinear Hamiltonian, governing quantum three-wave mixing and parametric amplification. Starting from a coherent pump and vacuum signal and idler, the calculation reorganizes the Heisenberg expansion into resummed depletion and return profiles, yielding directly evaluable expressions for all 1st-, 2nd- and 3rd-order correlations. The construction uses no parametric approximation or fitted parameters. Representative numerical benchmarks show errors of order $10^{-12}$ throughout the entire pump depletion, and below $10^{-3}$ across dozens of depletion-and-back-conversion cycles, up to the first total collapse of the oscillation. The first-depletion treatment additionally provides 4th-order correlations, accommodates bright squeezed-pump inputs and reveals phenomena important to future optical quantum technologies. The framework can be extended to higher moments.
summary: This paper provides a comprehensive, fully quantized theoretical treatment of parametric amplification and three-wave mixing. It derives exact analytic expressions for quantum correlations, successfully handling the complex physics of pump depletion without resorting to approximations. The results are vital for advancing quantum optical technologies by accurately predicting noise characteristics.
main_problem: The paper derives analytic expressions for observable dynamics under the fully quantized trilinear Hamiltonian governing quantum three-wave mixing and parametric amplification, especially when pump depletion occurs.
main_result: The analytic framework successfully calculates first-, second-, and third-order correlations without relying on parametric approximations, resolving complex quantum noise features like finite minimum squeezing.
method: The authors reorganize the Heisenberg expansion using Borel summation and define normalized moments to derive directly evaluable expressions for correlation functions.
model_or_system: The system models quantum three-wave mixing and parametric amplification, governed by a quantized trilinear Hamiltonian. The analysis tracks the evolution of quantum operators under pump depletion.
key_observables: First-, second-, and third-order correlations; Pump quadrature variances ($V_{X_c}, V_{Y_c}$); Signal-idler squeezing variance ($	ext{VEPR}$).
important_parameters: Pump depletion level ($\chi$), input squeezing parameters ($r, 	heta$), and the coupling constant ($g$).
main_assumptions: The method is designed to overcome limitations of previous work that used approximations or resulted in non-compact solutions; the analysis is restricted in later passages.
figures_summary: Figure 1 compares numerical evolution with corrected analytic results for pump population; Figure 2 shows $	ext{VEPR}$ vs. $\chi$ comparing different approximations; Figure 3 demonstrates how input squeezing controls third-order correlations.
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops the analytic framework by calculating moments, deriving expressions for correlations, and then presenting detailed mathematical machinery via index maps and polynomial fits to determine return profiles.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous, non-perturbative analytical tools to calculate quantum noise and correlations in nonlinear optical processes, which is crucial for understanding quantum light sources and quantum information processing.

Nu- merical evolution (blue solid), the leading analytic approxima- tion (green dashed), and the corrected analytic result (orange dashed) are shown through χ = 200. The corrected result re- solves the repeated conversion cycles and their decaying enve- lope. Its relative population error, ∆P = |Pnum−Pana|/Pnum, is of order 10−13 during the ﬁrst depletion and remains below 10−3 over the plotted interval. The error curves and detailed comparison are given in the SM; see also SM Fig. 3.

Black solid curves are evaluated from the resummed ﬁrst-depletion expressions; blue dashed curves give the undepleted quadratic result e−2χ. The red dotted line denotes vacuum noise. (a) Fixed α = 25, with time varied through 0 ≤χ ≤2 log(4α), on a linear vertical scale. The ﬁrst squeezing minimum is ﬁnite, and later conversion dynamics produce nonmonotonic noise. The interaction is ﬁxed at τ = 0.001, with θ = π and r = 0, 0.5, 1, 1.25 shown in black, blue, orange, and green, respectively. Vabc = −⟨XaXbδXc⟩in the convention of Eq. (1), where δXc = Xc −⟨Xc⟩. Stronger phase squeezing produces a negative interval followed by a sign reversal as α increases. The nonzero third-order central moment witnesses non-Gaussian correlations; its sign is set by the chosen quadrature phases.

The “best” solution has all corrections implemented (higher-order terms, passage interference and Poisson-clocks). The precise errors from numerical benchmark are shown in Figure 2 below.

Figure 2: Absolute errors in our solutions against numerical benchmark (the numerical results were obtained by directly diagonalizing the Hamiltonian). Error = ∆C = |Cnumerics −Canalytics|. (a) For the best solution (all corrections applied), the maximum absolute error during the ﬁrst depletion is 2.6 × 10−13; during the ﬁrst return it is 3.0 × 10−4. This is a great improvement from the leading proﬁle error, which reaches 0.012 at maximum. Note the “jump” in the blue curve at χ ≃10 occurs since the depletion proﬁle was calculated to 19 orders, while the return was calculated to 1 order, thus order-by-order matching was not possible.
